clue.text: Two beastly males providing stiff fabric

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, the first of the two male beasts
a ram is a male sheep, the second of the two

explanation.surface: Two male animals are somehow the source of a stiff cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two beastly males' is one phrase that supplies both pieces: a male deer followed by a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse cotton or linen cloth stiffened with size, used in bookbinding and hat-making.

clue.text: Hope and Crosby going up and down

parts.note: Bob Hope, the American comedian
Bing Crosby, the singer and Hope's film partner in the Road movies

explanation.surface: Bob Hope and Bing Crosby, the famous comedy duo, are bouncing about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surnames stand for the first names that went with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bobbing moves repeatedly upward and downward, like a cork floating on water.

clue.text: Present flower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the present time, contemporary
second meaning: something that flows, a stream of water or air

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom but is read as 'one that flows', a crossword favourite for a river or stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means happening now, and as a noun it is a moving body of water that flows.

clue.text: Tears as leading character in romance dies

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of romance
something that dies comes to an end

explanation.surface: Someone weeps as the heroine of a love story perishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping, but here it is the verb rhyming with 'bears': rips.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart violently, so rends works as a synonym for tears in the ripping sense.

clue.text: "True men" is false!

indicators.note: something false is not what it appears, so the letters before it are not in their true order

parts.note: the quoted words plus the following word supply the letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation denouncing a claim that some men are loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: rebels on a ship are anything but true men to their captain, so calling them so is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers are sailors or soldiers who rise against their officers, the very opposite of loyal followers.

clue.text: Play with numbers

parts.note: surface reading: toy with figures, as an accountant fiddling sums might
setter's reading: a stage show in which the numbers are songs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' sounds like arithmetic, but in the theatre a number is a song or routine, and 'Play' is a noun, a stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage production built around songs and dance routines is a show of that genre, like Oklahoma or Cats.

clue.text: Old man in one sort of tree has to climb another

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading from bottom to top, so the order flips
one item sitting inside another means placing it within the tree's letters

parts.note: the elm is a common tree
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: An elderly man up one tree has to scramble up a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, climbing means the letters are read from the bottom upward, so the finished container is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree in its own right, distinct from the elm, so it is the other kind referred to.

clue.text: Marine creature lookin' round the bend?

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: lookin' is searchin', with the dropped g kept dropped
a U-bend is a pipe bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A sea animal seems to be peering around a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in lookin' signals the same clipped ending on the synonym; U goes in after SEA. A U-bend is the curved trap pipe under a sink.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea urchin is a spiny, globe-shaped echinoderm found on rocky sea beds.

clue.text: Leader in a pact that's been arranged

indicators.note: arranged letters have been put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chief figures in an agreement that has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the leader inside the pact, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain heads a team, ship or army company, so the word is a common synonym for one in charge.

clue.text: Cough mixture was our connection, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: was our connection means joined us together

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a bottle of cough medicine is what brought them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a thick syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough or sore throat.

clue.text: Titleholder, excluding a single Tory leader

parts.note: to bar is to exclude, as in 'bar none'
a single item is one

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so the opening letter alone is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A titled aristocrat shuns the one Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' reads as an instruction to remove letters, but it is a synonym, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking just below a baron, styled Sir.

clue.text: Take on US prison where child may be behind bars

definitions.text: where child may be behind bars

parts.note: to take on an opponent is to play them
the pen, short for penitentiary, is American slang for jail

explanation.surface: Someone tackles an American jail, where a youngster might be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' suggests prison, but the bars are the sides of an infant's enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure with barred sides in which a toddler can play safely.

clue.text: Fashionable perfume, fundamentally

parts.note: in means in fashion
an essence is a concentrated scent

explanation.surface: A trendy fragrance is described as being basically so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at bottom or in its essential nature, the same as basically.

clue.text: Severely criticise traditional Sunday lunch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to attack someone harshly, as a critic might
second meaning: the joint of meat cooked in the oven for the British weekend meal

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Sunday lunch is traditionally a joint of meat cooked in the oven with potatoes and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to lambast someone, and the noun is the meat dish served at the weekly family meal.

clue.text: Twig, for example, brought back by bird

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way, so it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A twig serving as an example is carried home by a bird for its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a stick but is the informal verb meaning to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig something is to suddenly understand it, and the colloquial phrase for grasping a point means the same.

clue.text: He's among group of stars in reference book

indicators.note: one thing among others sits in their midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: Taurus, the Bull, is a constellation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man appears among a constellation listed in an astronomy reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference work listing words grouped by meaning, with their synonyms.

clue.text: A net helps wild animals

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trapping creatures in the wild is easier with a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild animals' reads as one phrase, but 'wild' is the anagram signal and only 'animals' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are large mammals, a specific example of the general class of beasts.

clue.text: Try shuffling over a dune

indicators.note: shuffling mixes things up like a pack of cards, so the order changes

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted walker attempts to trudge across a sand hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to attempt or make an effort, the same as to try.

clue.text: Down with legal document constraining journalists

indicators.note: constraining holds something in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: A court order restricting reporters is being brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction, but it means low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is feeling sad or low, which is what being depressed means.

clue.text: Expired time after amusement in December

indicators.note: coming after means placed at the end, following the rest
something in a month sits inside it, so one piece goes within

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation
amusement is fun
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Some period of festive enjoyment in December has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expired' looks like a clue to a lapsed ticket or deadline, but it means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct is dead or no longer operating, so it has expired.

clue.text: Obtain professional medical treatment

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a cure is a remedy or treatment

explanation.surface: A patient gets expert medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to acquire or get hold of it, often with some effort.

clue.text: Clegg's cuts?

parts.note: surface reading: spending cuts made by the former Liberal Democrat leader and UK Deputy Prime Minister
setter's reading: more than one of the politician's first name, which as a common noun also means small cuts

explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led Britain's Liberal Democrats and was Deputy Prime Minister in the coalition that made austerity cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Small notches or scratches made with a blade are cuts, and the word doubles as plural of Clegg's first name.

clue.text: Princess gets stuck into pink drink

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means being lodged inside it

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
Di, Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A royal tucks into a pink beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets stuck into' suggests eagerly starting on the drink; it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit-flavoured concentrate diluted with water, or a liqueur, a type of beverage.

clue.text: Cat sees bats about one in the morning

indicators.note: being about something means going around it, enclosing the rest
bats is slang for crazy, so the word before it goes haywire into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A cat spots some bats flying around early one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the creatures the cat sees, but it is slang for mad, signalling the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic cat with blue eyes and dark points, an example of the definition.

clue.text: I'd quit the Sunshine State for this girl

indicators.note: to quit a place is to leave it, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: the Sunshine State is the nickname of Florida
I'd with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone says they'd leave Florida behind for the sake of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ID from FLORIDA leaves FLOR plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is a female given name, so it stands for a girl, as such names often do in crosswords.

clue.text: Place to eat pastry that's brought back to Rhode Island area

indicators.note: something brought back is returned the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with filling
taken as written
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
a is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A restaurant's dessert is being sent back to a region of Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, a place where people go to dine.

clue.text: Not a lonely part for a hooker?

indicators.note: part of a phrase is a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the three words from the end of the first

explanation.surface: Asks whether a role for a prostitute is anything but solitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' suggests a prostitute or a rugby forward, but here means a bird of prey that hooks with its claws; the definition reads as 'something for a hooker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey, the tool such a bird uses to grip and hook prey.

clue.text: Belgian city ignoring an ass

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Belgian city snubs a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' looks like the animal but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, so an informal synonym for a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Non-combatant lacking distinctive features

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country taking no side in a war
second meaning: plain and bland, like a colour such as beige

explanation.definitionFit: A neutral state stays out of a conflict, and a neutral colour or style has no strong character.

clue.text: Former opener for Essex enters punctually

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it

parts.note: punctually means on time

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Essex

explanation.surface: A former opening batsman for Essex walks out to bat right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county cricket team, and an opener is a batsman who starts the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means having been so in the past, such as a one-time champion, just as former does.

clue.text: Traitor's initial motive for his crime

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter of a name or word

parts.note: the first letter of Traitor
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: Asks what first drove a traitor to commit his offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the traitor, so the definition is the traitor's crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the specific offence that makes someone a traitor.

clue.text: Sign of life after sappers drive back

indicators.note: placing something after another means it comes second in the sequence

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a pulse shows the heart is beating

explanation.surface: Army engineers check for a heartbeat before pushing an enemy back.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in the British Army they form the Royal Engineers, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to force the attackers to retreat, the same as driving them back.
